title: Redwood POC scoping with Ridgepoint Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot. Discussed SOC 2 / ISO needs, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs and KMS integration, data residency and VPC options. Agreed success criteria (ingestion accuracy, X TPS, latency <200ms p95), benchmark plan and 3-week timeline to pilot kickoff. Next steps: send SOW + security pack, schedule bench run, and internal stakeholder review.
next_steps: Sofia: send pilot SOW, pricing and security pack (by 2027-12-03)
Ethan: schedule benchmark run and prepare workload script (by 2027-12-07)
Ridgepoint: confirm legal / procurement review timeline (by 2027-12-06)
All: pilot kickoff call week of 2027-12-13
action_items: Sofia Martinez: Email SOC 2/ISO artifact pack + data flow diagram - due 2027-12-03
Ethan Cole: Create benchmark workload (concurrency 50, 1k tokens/request average) and run internal smoke tests - due 2027-12-07
Anita Patel: Share sample dataset and anonymization checklist - due 2027-12-06

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 minutes | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Laura (Ridgepoint VP Product), Marcus (Ridgepoint Head of Security), Anita (Ridgepoint Eng)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect): Scoping for a security-first pilot of Redwood inference. Focus on SOC 2 / ISO 27001 requirements, SSO via SAML, RBAC, audit log retention, KMS key control, VPC/private deployment option, data residency. Benchmarks: throughput and latency targets, sample workload size (tokens/request), metrics to collect. Timeline: agreement to kick off mid-December, bench runs in early December.

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll run about 45-60 minutes, thanks for making time. quick intros?
[00:14] Laura: hi, Laura Chen, VP Product at Ridgepoint, leading the pilots for docs automation project.
[00:21] Marcus: Marcus Green, security lead, will own compliance sign-off.
[00:26] Anita: Anita Patel, eng manager, I'll help with dataset and infra.
[00:31] Sofia: awesome, and I'm Sofia Martinez, account exec, with Ethan Cole, our solutions engineer, who's gonna cover benchmarks and sizing.
[00:40] Ethan: hi all, uh, thanks. quick note - we have a security deck and artifact pack, i'll share link after - the link's in chat, Security deck (link: https://redwood.ai/sec-deck) - it has SOC 2 scope, ISO certs, KMS notes.
[01:02] Marcus: great, quick question - are you SOC 2 type II? we need the report and scope details. sometimes vendors say 'SOC2' but scope matters.
[01:14] Sofia: yes we're SOC 2 Type II for infra and platform, and we can share the SOC pack, also we have ISO 27001 cert, we can share certificate and scope doc.
[01:26] Marcus: ok, good. second - SSO: we use SAML 2.0 with Okta. can you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[01:38] Ethan: yes, SAML 2.0 supported, SCIM for provisioning is available on enterprise plans, we can enable RBAC roles: admin, dev, viewer, and custom roles. setup requires an SP/IDP metadata exchange.
[01:52] Laura: for the pilot we need RBAC so our data scientists can't access PHI logs.
[01:58] Sofia: understood, we'll document role mappings.
[02:05] Anita: on audit logs - what's the retention and granularity? we need immutable logs showing who requested model inference, payload hashes, timestamps, and response codes.
[02:19] Ethan: we capture token-level billing events, request/response IDs, user ID, and timestamps. audit logs can be exported to your S3 or to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch pipeline; retention configurable. note - for hosted, default retention is 90 days but we can extend for enterprise.
[02:39] Marcus: and encryption? at rest and in transit, plus KMS integration for customer-managed keys?
[02:46] Sofia: yes, TLS everywhere, at-rest encryption with our KMS; enterprise private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key.
[02:58] Marcus: good. also data residency - we need EU region processing for certain datasets.
[03:05] Ethan: we can route to EU region, and for private deployments you can run in your VPC on-prem.
[03:12] Laura: ok these cover security questions. next, success criteria - what do you suggest for the pilot?
[03:20] Sofia: from other health pilots we use a mix of functional and non-functional: functional: extraction accuracy on our labeled set (F1 > 0.85), hallucination rate under 3% on sampled prompts; non-functional: latency p95 < 200ms for short prompts, throughput target of X requests per second we size to your peak.
[03:40] Anita: for our workload, bursts up to 50 concurrent requests, average 1k tokens per request when doing summaries. peak approx 200 reqs/minute.
[03:50] Ethan: ok, so 50 concurrency, we'll recommend either dedicated pool or dedicated nodes in private mode, to meet p95 <200ms for 1k tokens depends on model size/quantization. we'll propose a benchmark matrix.
[04:05] Marcus: what's the expected cost tradeoff for dedicated vs hosted? security-wise we prefer dedicated but cost is a factor.
[04:15] Sofia: Dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable throughput and isolation, pricing is monthly committed; hosted is pay-as-you-go but shared infra. For pilot we typically run a short dedicated burst or a private demo env to validate SLOs.
[04:30] Laura: timeline question - procurement and legal need docs. procurement slowness is a risk; we want pilot kickoff before year-end. possible?
[04:40] Sofia: we can aim for kickoff mid-December; action: i'll send SOW + security pack within a couple business days.
[04:50] Marcus: procurement will need SOC 2, ISO cert, data processing addendum (DPA), and potentially a subprocessors list.
[04:58] Sofia: noted, we'll include DPA and subprocessors list.
[05:05] Anita: benchmarking - what metrics will you collect and what do you need from us?
[05:12] Ethan: we need a representative request script: concurrency profile (50 concurrent), payload sizes (tokens per request - sample average 1k, peaks 3k), expected latency SLO (p95 <200ms), target throughput (200 rpm). we'll run three bench scenarios: smoke (10 users), steady-state (50 conc), burst (150 conc) to validate autoscale. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
[05:44] Laura: can you run the bench inside our VPC or do you need egress to Redwood hosted?
[05:52] Ethan: for private pilot we can run a bench from within your VPC using our private connector, otherwise hosted bench runs from our infra. for security concerns, private bench is preferred.
[06:05] Marcus: will request payloads contain PHI? if yes we need to ensure data minimization and retention policies.
[06:13] Anita: we'll anonymize PHI for the pilot, but may provide synthetically generated examples. we'll share checklist.
[06:20] Ethan: perfect - also for metrics we can hash payloads in transit to keep traceability without storing raw text.
[06:28] Laura: how long is pilot usually?
[06:31] Sofia: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: week 0 onboarding (security & infra), week 1 bench & baseline, weeks 2-3 iteration and tuning, final week for evaluation and decision. we can compress to 3 weeks if procurement moves fast.
[06:46] Marcus: procurement likely needs 2 weeks to review docs. so realistic kickoff mid-december, bench early Dec - that timeline seems tight.
[06:55] Sofia: agreed, action to get docs fast.
[07:00] Ethan: on the model side - which model family do you want to evaluate? smaller quantized for latency or larger for accuracy?
[07:08] Laura: we prefer accuracy for extraction but need reasonable latency. would you recommend a medium-sized model with 8-bit quantization?
[07:16] Ethan: yes, we can recommend a quantized variant that keeps F1 high while reducing memory and improving throughput. Part of bench is testing quantization profiles.
[07:25] Anita: is there a way to reproduce logs for audit, like immutability or append-only?
[07:31] Ethan: audit logs are write-once in our system; for dedicated/private deployments we can configure immutable S3 buckets or send to your SIEM for long-term retention.
[07:40] Marcus: retention period - can you commit to 7 years? that might be long. we probably need 1-7 years depending on regulation.
[07:49] Sofia: long-term retention is configurable but may require additional storage SLAs; we'll note that as a procurement discussion point.
[07:58] Laura: what about redaction? can Redwood redact sensitive spans before storing?
[08:04] Ethan: we have pre-storage redaction rules and can strip PII on ingest via rules or customer-side preprocessing. for compliance, customer-managed redaction is recommended.
[08:15] Marcus: ok, let's document that.
[08:18] (longer section where Ethan walks through benchmark matrix - transcribed imperfectly)
[08:20] Ethan: so benchmark matrix - Scenario A: 10 conc, 1k tokens, target p95 < 200ms. Scenario B: 50 conc steady, Scenario C: burst 150 conc for 30 seconds. collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util. we'll also test warm cache vs cold cache, and KV cache effectiveness.
[08:53] Anita: how will you simulate our prompt shapes? we will provide a sample set of 200 prompts plus a generated long-form set.
[09:00] Ethan: perfect, please provide sample in CSV; we'll need metadata columns: prompt_type, avg_tokens.
[09:07] Laura: about billing - do you provide an estimate for pilot cost? we need a ballpark for procurement.
[09:13] Sofia: yes, i'll include a pilot estimate in SOW: estimate for dedicated short-term nodes + bench costs; if hosted, estimate pay-as-you-go.
[09:22] Marcus: legal will likely ask for subprocessors and data flow diagram - can you include a diagram showing where data is cached and how KMS is used?
[09:30] Sofia: yes we'll attach data flow diagram and subprocessors list.
[09:34] Laura: benchmarks - success criteria recap?
[09:37] Sofia: functional: Extraction F1 >= 0.85 on your labeled set, hallucination <3% on sampled prompts. Non-functional: p95 latency <200ms for 1k tokens (or best-effort depending on model), throughput to support peaks (50 concurrent steady), and predictable error rates under 1%.
[09:56] Anita: what about rollback / graceful degradation? if the model falls back what happens?
[10:02] Ethan: we support routing policies and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant; during pilot we'll test fallback scenarios and monitor for quality regressions.
[10:12] Marcus: extra ask - we require a SOC 2 attestation that includes log monitoring for privileged access. can you show separation of duties?
[10:21] Sofia: yes, access controls and privileged logging are part of SOC 2 scope; we'll include sample reports.
[10:29] (some cross-talk, filler - got slightly garbled)
[10:35] Speaker 1: uh-huh, yeah, ok -
[10:38] Ethan: next, timeline specifics: we propose 3 tracks - Security docs delivery (48-72 hours), technical bench prep (1 week), pilot kickoff mid-Dec.
[10:48] Laura: procurement and legal internal reviews could add 1-2 weeks, Marcus will coordinate.
[10:54] Marcus: yes, I'll flag security and legal, plan to review by 12/06.
[10:59] Sofia: action items recap - i'll send SOW + artifact pack by Friday (2027-12-03). Ethan will prepare bench scripts and sample runner.
[11:08] Ethan: noted, i'll also include a runnable dockerized bench script we can run in your VPC if you'd like.
[11:15] Anita: for the bench runner, we'll provide a small k8s namespace to run from; network peering will be arranged.
[11:22] Ethan: good, private connector details - we'll need a service account and egress rules.
[11:27] Laura: ok, any other questions on compliance?
[11:30] Marcus: one more - does Redwood support separation of logs by customer with cryptographic signing?
[11:36] Ethan: we can sign logs and store signatures alongside logs, and export them. for private deployments you can own the signing keys.
[11:44] Laura: great.
[11:46] (brief pause)
[11:50] Sofia: wrap up - recap success criteria, bench plan, artifacts to send, timeline target.
[11:56] Laura: sounds good.
[11:58] Sofia: ok will follow up with SOW + security pack. thanks everyone.
[12:02] Meeting end / transcript notes: transcription may mis-attribute names or slightly garble technical terms (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V catch'), check attached security deck for canonical wording.

References shared in call: Security deck (https://redwood.ai/sec-deck), Pilot SOW template (link sent after call), Bench runner repo (private link to be shared).

Recap / Next steps: 1) Redwood to send SOW + SOC 2 + ISO docs + DPA + subprocessors list by 2027-12-03. 2) Ridgepoint to confirm procurement timeline and provide sample prompts + anonymized dataset by 2027-12-06. 3) Redwood SE to run bench (private connector) week of 2027-12-07 and report results.
